edits.old: - `org-topologies-primer-2025-stakeholder-engagement.md`, Alexey Krivitsky, Craig Larman & Roland Flemm (*Strategic Org Design: The Primer*, Org Topologies™ 2025 Edition). Engagement framing for org-change initiatives. Core principle: "people have to own – not rent – their change." OT's named archetypes (CAPS, WHOLE, TASKS) as framework-agnostic engagement vocabulary. MADE method (MAP, ASSESS, DESIGN, ELEVATE) structured as co-creation rather than rollout: MAP step requires going to the hands-on workplace; ASSESS step as co-discovering mismatch in shared vocabulary; ELEVATE step as stakeholder-owned Katas. Framework-first adoption as a named disengagement failure mode (cargo-cult mentality, Religious Wars, no buy-in). Multi-level engagement as a structural requirement (strategic leadership, HR/Finance policy owners, group/team structures, individual contributors). Resource Topology's "people as resources" framing named as a low-ownership, low-voice pattern. Periodic re-mapping as the sustaining engagement rhythm. **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — Share-Alike and Non-Commercial obligations propagate.** Narrower than the load-bearing engagement texts (Liberating Structures, FLO Facilitation Guide) — strongest in the org-change-initiative design context; pairs with the OpenStax Organizational Behavior distillation for the psychology-of-change elaboration the Primer references but does not provide.
